labware.title: The wrong kind of plate: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat is a flat plate, and PCR setup needs a PCR plate or PCR strips
labware.explanation: The plate map says the technique is PCR setup, which needs a PCR plate or PCR strips as its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 3, load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the reaction can never be run. The plate map checks what each well holds, not what plate it is.
labware.fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.

1. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 12 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at
least)
   line 63:  p300.aspirate(12, component_block["A3"])
   At line 63 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 12 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul. A
   pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong amount, or nothing, and
   the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator passes the move. Wells:
   well A3 in slot 4.
   Affected: well A3 in slot 4.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [352f94cde52a]

2. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 5: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 98:  p300.aspirate(23, reservoir["A1"])
   At line 98 the p300_single_gen2 draws 23 ul from well A1 in slot 5 with its tip 1 mm
   above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 178 ul, which in this NEST 12 Well
   Reservoir 15 mL reaches only 0.85 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this
   line did it 6 times, after 42 times in the liquid; 138 ul of air in all). The simulator
   does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 6 wells filled from these draws got
   air instead of liquid.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 5.
   Also reached 6 other wells: wells D7, D8, D9, D10, D11 and D12 in slot 3.
   Fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 258 ul in it for the surface to
   reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube
   lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   [b1bd3600001e]

3. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 47 stocks
   line 105:  p20.aspirate(2, template_well)
   At line 105 the tip went into template 2 (tube A2 in slot 6), template 3 (tube A3 in slot
   6), template 4 (tube A4 in slot 6), template 5 (tube A5 in slot 6) and 43 more while it
   still carried template 1 (tube A1 in slot 6), template 2 (tube A2 in slot 6), template 3
   (tube A3 in slot 6), template 4 (tube A4 in slot 6) and 43 more from an earlier step
   (this line did it 47 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in
   the next liquid it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there.
   Liquid drawn from them then took the unwanted material along into 47 other wells: wells
   A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 39 more in slot 3.
   Affected: tubes A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2, B3 and 15 more in slot 6; tubes A1, A2, A3,
   A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in slot 7.
   Also reached 47 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 39 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 105 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [cf2a80b28625]

4. WARNING COLD-MODULE-NEVER-SET: A temperature module was loaded but never set
   line 59:  p300.aspirate(240, component_block["A1"])
   At line 59 the robot draws from wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 4, on a
   temperature module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays at room
   temperature until `set_temperature` is called, so buffer (carrier), dntp (reagent), fwd
   primer (reagent), polymerase (reagent) and 2 more sat on a block that was never cold; the
   robot pipetted there 9 times over the run. The person setting up the deck sees a module
   and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 4.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 4.
   Fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from Opentrons 24
   Well Aluminum Block with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap in slot 4, and `temp_module.deactivate()` at
   the end.
   Source: Opentrons, temperature module: at room temperature until set_temperature, which
   blocks
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/temperature_module.html
   Source: Thermo Fisher T4 ligase manual: keep on ice, use within minutes
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/t4dnaligase_1U_man.pdf
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   [64d25f6da49b]

5. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: polymerase (well A3 in slot 4)
   line 63:  p300.aspirate(12, component_block["A3"])
   At line 63 the tip went into polymerase (well A3 in slot 4) while it still carried buffer
   (well A1 in slot 4) and dntp (well A2 in slot 4) from an earlier step. A tip that has
   touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now
   holds material that does not belong there. The protocol does not draw from it again, so
   this run is not harmed, but what is left in the stock is no longer clean for the next
   run.
   Affected: well A3 in slot 4.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 63 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [1c794f3cd9a0]

6. WARNING ENZYME-BEFORE-DILUENT: An enzyme was added before the water: polymerase
   line 64:  p300.dispense(12, reservoir["A1"])
   At line 64 the robot put polymerase into well A1 in slot 5. Take well A1 in slot 5: at
   that moment it held 264 ul, only 240 ul of it water or buffer, and the water came
   afterwards, at line 72, to make the 948 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built on.
   An enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol and is meant to be the last thing into a reaction,
   after the water and the buffer have brought the well to the right dilution. Dropped into
   neat buffer or a dry well it meets many times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme
   then cuts at the wrong places (star activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed
   template.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 5.
   Fix: Reorder the additions to well A1 in slot 5: water and buffer first, then the sample,
   then polymerase last. Or make a master mix of water, buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix
   it, and hand it out.
   Source: Thermo Fisher: restriction enzyme key considerations (the enzyme is the final
   component)
           https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/cloning/cloning-learning-center/invitrogen-school-of-molecular-biology/molecular-cloning/restriction-enzymes/restriction-enzyme-key-considerations.html
   Source: Promega: restriction enzyme resource (add the enzyme last; glycerol and star
   activity)
           https://www.promega.com/resources/guides/nucleic-acid-analysis/restriction-enzyme-resource/
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   Source: Qiagen: critical factors for successful real-time PCR (order of addition)
           https://www.gene-quantification.de/qiagen-qpcr-sample-assay-tech-guide-2010.pdf
   [b6f401272ee3]

7. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: fwd primer (well A4 in slot 4)
   line 65:  p300.aspirate(60, component_block["A4"])
   At line 65 the tip went into fwd primer (well A4 in slot 4) while it still carried buffer
   (well A1 in slot 4), dntp (well A2 in slot 4) and polymerase (well A3 in slot 4) from an
   earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid
   it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. The protocol
   drew from it again afterwards, but only into wells that were given that material on
   purpose anyway, so this run is not harmed. What is left in the stock is no longer clean
   for the next run.
   Affected: well A4 in slot 4.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 65 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing

   [e383f8f3284f]

10. WARNING MIX-BEFORE-DRAW: Liquid drawn from well A1 in slot 5 before it was mixed: added
at line 76, drawn at line 98
   line 76:  p300.dispense(108, reservoir["A1"])
   At line 76 liquid was added to well A1 in slot 5, which already held a different liquid.
   At line 98 liquid was drawn out of it again, and the well was never mixed in between. Two
   liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the tip drew is not at
   the concentration you calculated. In a dilution series every later step inherits the
   error.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 5.
   Also reached 42 other wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 34 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix the well after the addition at line 76: `mix_after=(5, volume)` in a transfer,
   or `pipette.mix(5, volume, well)`. Integra suggests about 5 cycles at about 80% of the
   volume in the well.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   Source: Svec et al. 2015: how good is a PCR efficiency estimate
           https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4822216/
   [74ec2047883a]

12. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 42 wells of dntp and polymerase with a
sample
   line 99:  p300.dispense(23, reaction_well)
   At line 99 the robot starts putting dntp and polymerase into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL
   Flat (slot 3), and 42 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate
   holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is
   contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing
   on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8
   and 34 more in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 34 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 0.723776 ul of dntp and polymerase and 2 ul of
   water in place of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [f7970c53d716]

13. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 42 wells never mixed after template 1, template 2, template 3,
template 4 and 38 more went in (8% of the well)
   line 106:  p20.dispense(2, reaction_well)
   At line 106 the robot added template 1, template 2, template 3, template 4 and 38 more to
   wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 34 more in slot 3, which already held buffer,
   dntp, polymerase, fwd primer and 2 more (this line did it 42 times). The addition was 8%
   of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two
   liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at
   the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before
   cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 34 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 34 more in slot 3 after line 106:
   `mix_after=(5, 20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20, well)`, with the volume about
   80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [632da54c356c]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: Liquid drawn from well A1 in slot 5 before it was mixed: added at line 76, drawn at line 98
findings.explanation: At line 76 liquid was added to well A1 in slot 5, which already held a different liquid. At line 98 liquid was drawn out of it again, and the well was never mixed in between. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the tip drew is not at the concentration you calculated. In a dilution series every later step inherits the error.
findings.fix: Mix the well after the addition at line 76: `mix_after=(5, volume)` in a transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, volume, well)`. Integra suggests about 5 cycles at about 80% of the volume in the well.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: dntp (well A2 in slot 4)
findings.explanation: At line 61 the tip went into dntp (well A2 in slot 4) while it still carried buffer (well A1 in slot 4) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. The protocol does not draw from it again, so this run is not harmed, but what is left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 61 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: No no-template control: 42 wells of dntp and polymerase with a sample
findings.explanation: At line 99 the robot starts putting dntp and polymerase into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 3), and 42 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 34 more in slot 3.
findings.fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 0.723776 ul of dntp and polymerase and 2 ul of water in place of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.

findings.title: 42 wells never mixed after template 1, template 2, template 3, template 4 and 38 more went in (8% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 106 the robot added template 1, template 2, template 3, template 4 and 38 more to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 34 more in slot 3, which already held buffer, dntp, polymerase, fwd primer and 2 more (this line did it 42 times). The addition was 8% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
findings.fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 34 more in slot 3 after line 106: `mix_after=(5, 20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
